messages:
Anya: quick RFC follow-up — proposing we slim the adapter contract between hosted/dedicated/private. idea: stop passing a full model manifest by default, instead expose a small capability hint surface and allow opt-in full manifests for migrations.
Marco: +1 to smaller surface. main worry is secrets/tokens and observability hooks. how do we preserve telemetry without full pass-through?
Devon: can we keep a stable probe endpoint that returns capabilities + telemetry endpoints? that should let us route and still collect metrics.
Sasha: sketch of a 3-phase rollout:
- phase 1: define minimal capability shape and probe (non-breaking)
- phase 2: adapters start honoring capability hints and log deprecation when they still accept full manifest
- phase 3: flip default to capabilities-only, full manifest behind flag for 6 months then remove
Anya: @Sasha that ordering sounds right. also we should add explicit opt-in for "secret forwarding" so adapters can't blindly request KMS keys.
Marco: here's a minimal capability example we discussed, so implementers have something concrete:
```json
{
  "capabilities": ["streaming","kv_cache","batched_infer"],
  "max_sequence": 4096,
  "preferred_precision": "int8",
  "auth_kind": "token"
}
```
Devon: +1. small nit: include a "feature_versions" map so we can roll capability schema forward without breaking old adapters.
Sasha: tradeoffs to call out in RFC blurb:
- pro: dramatically smaller control-plane payloads and faster probes
- con: adapters must implement fallback logic for missing manifest fields (complexity)
- pro: easier to reason about upgrade compatibility across hosted/dedicated/private
- con: temporary extra code path for legacy adapters during migration
Anya: rollout ops: canary by tenant tier (free > paid > enterprise) and route to legacy adapter if compatibility check fails. telemetry tag on request for which path used.
Marco: ops question — what about Dedicated where customers expect data isolation? we must ensure capability surface contains no PII or model prompts. mark that in spec.
Devon: agreed. also add "no_secret_proxy" flag default true; explicit allow list for enterprise accounts if they sign DPA and enable via console.
infra-bot: RFC doc: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026/adapter-contract-slimdown (added inline diff + open comment thread) :eyes:
Sasha: next steps: 1) update RFC with minimal JSON shape + migration plan 2) create an integration test that asserts probe-only path works end-to-end 3) schedule canary rollout playbook w/ SRE
Anya: I'll update the RFC and ping eng-runtime and eng-platform for review. thanks team — short follow-up sync tomorrow? :calendar: 
Marco: yes, 10am PT works for me.
Devon: added to calendar.
Sasha: i'll prep the integration test checklist.
